library(dplyr)

## What this compares

The influence-function (IF) PEHE score of Alaa & van der Schaar (2019),
`me_metrics.R::calc_infl_score()`, needs a surrogate CATE τ̃ to correct
around. The study scores it with two, and this report asks which one picks
the better candidate:

| score | formula | surrogate |
|---|---|---|
| **IF, T-learner** (`inflt`) | `calc_infl_score()` | plug-in τ̃ = μ̂₁ − μ̂₀ from the scoring pipeline's per-arm outcome models. The IF score the thesis reports |
| **IF, pseudo-outcome** (`infl`) | the same | the AIPW pseudo-outcome φ, built from the same μ̂₀, μ̂₁ and π̂ |
| **DR risk** (`dr`) | mean (φ − τ̂)² | – (reference) |

The Curth & van der Schaar (2023) appendix version is not scored: the formula
printed there is a typo, and their code uses the 2019 formula.

What to expect. The surrogate enters the candidate-dependent part of the
score only through 2(W − π)·τ̃·τ̂. With τ̃ = φ, that term also gets φ's
residual correction, which is mean zero only where μ̂ is right. So the
pseudo-outcome surrogate should, on average, pick the same way as the
T-learner, but with more noise.

All scores here are from the **CV (`cv_shared`) arm** of the strategies tree:
the scoring nuisance is fit on the candidate's own `V − 1` training folds and
predicted on its held-out fold. The main figures use the estimated (trimmed)
propensity, and the fixed π = 0.5 versions are in the appendix. Every score,
and true PEHE, is a loss: lower is better.

The simulation results are read straight from `me_strat_metrics.RDS`
(`me_metrics.R strategies`), the same scores `me_results.qmd` and the thesis
tables use. The population check in section 5 is from
`me_infl_investigation.R`.

```{r data}
strat_path <- file.path(
  dirname(here()), "results", "correlated", "model_evaluation_strategies"
)
inv_path <- file.path(
  dirname(here()), "results", "correlated", "model_evaluation", "investigation"
)

ARM <- "cv_shared"

metrics <- readRDS(file.path(strat_path, "me_strat_metrics.RDS"))
population <- readRDS(file.path(inv_path, "population.RDS"))

scenario_labels <- c(
  `1` = "Null",
  `2` = "Simple",
  `3` = "Complex",
  `4` = "Non-linear"
)

score_labels <- c(
  inflt = "IF, T-learner",
  infl = "IF, pseudo-outcome",
  dr = "DR risk"
)

pipeline_labels <- c(xgb = "XGBoost", automl = "AutoML")

# me_metrics.R names every score column <score_type>_<arm>_<pipeline>, the
# score type carrying the propensity regime as a trailing "05" (inflt05,
# dr05, ...)
score_pattern <- paste0(
  "^(", paste(names(score_labels), collapse = "|"), ")(05)?_",
  ARM, "_(", paste(names(pipeline_labels), collapse = "|"), ")$"
)

# one row per (scenario, n, run, model, pipeline, score, pi regime)
scores <- metrics %>%
  select(scenario, n, run, model, true_pehe, mu1_mse, matches(score_pattern)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    matches(score_pattern),
    names_to = c("score", "pi_regime", "pipeline"),
    names_pattern = score_pattern,
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pi_regime = ifelse(pi_regime == "05", "fixed", "estimated"),
    score = factor(score_labels[score], levels = unname(score_labels)),
    scenario = factor(
      scenario_labels[as.character(scenario)],
      levels = unname(scenario_labels)
    ),
    n = factor(n, levels = sort(unique(n))),
    pipeline = factor(
      pipeline_labels[pipeline],
      levels = unname(pipeline_labels)
    )
  )

# per run and score, as me_selection() ranks: the candidates with a finite
# score and truth, regret against the best of them
perf <- scores %>%
  filter(is.finite(value), is.finite(true_pehe)) %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, run, pipeline, score, pi_regime) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  summarise(
    candidates = n(),
    spearman = suppressWarnings(cor(value, true_pehe, method = "spearman")),
    spearman_mu1 = suppressWarnings(
      cor(value, mu1_mse, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
    ),
    top1 = model[which.min(value)] == model[which.min(true_pehe)],
    pick = as.character(model[which.min(value)]),
    regret = true_pehe[which.min(value)] - min(true_pehe),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mcse_mean <- function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))

# mean +/- Monte Carlo SE over runs, per (scenario, n, pipeline, score, pi)
perf_summary <- perf %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, pipeline, score, pi_regime) %>%
  summarise(
    runs = n(),
    mean_regret = mean(regret),
    mcse_regret = mcse_mean(regret),
    mean_rho = mean(spearman, na.rm = TRUE),
    mcse_rho = mcse_mean(spearman),
    mean_rho_mu1 = mean(spearman_mu1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mcse_rho_mu1 = mcse_mean(spearman_mu1),
    mean_top1 = mean(top1),
    mcse_top1 = sqrt(mean_top1 * (1 - mean_top1) / runs),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# expected regret of ignoring every score and picking a candidate uniformly at
# random - the floor a useful score has to beat
random_baseline <- scores %>%
  filter(is.finite(true_pehe)) %>%
  distinct(scenario, n, run, model, true_pehe) %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, run) %>%
  summarise(random_regret = mean(true_pehe) - min(true_pehe), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(scenario, n) %>%
  summarise(random_regret = mean(random_regret), .groups = "drop")

# the two surrogates head to head, per run: T-learner minus pseudo-outcome
head_to_head <- perf %>%
  filter(score %in% score_labels[c("inflt", "infl")]) %>%
  mutate(score = names(score_labels)[match(score, score_labels)]) %>%
  select(scenario, n, run, pipeline, pi_regime, score, regret, spearman, pick) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = score,
    values_from = c(regret, spearman, pick)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(regret_inflt), !is.na(regret_infl)) %>%
  mutate(
    regret_diff = regret_inflt - regret_infl,
    spearman_diff = spearman_inflt - spearman_infl,
    same_pick = pick_inflt == pick_infl
  )
```

```{r plot-helpers, include=FALSE}
house_theme <- theme_bw() +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    strip.text = element_text(colour = "black")
  )

score_colours <- setNames(
  as.character(paletteer::paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe", length(score_labels))),
  unname(score_labels)
)

selection_plot <- function(df, mean_col, mcse_col, title, ylab,
                           baseline = NULL, hline = NULL, alpha = 0.05) {
  z <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      est = .data[[mean_col]],
      lo = est - z * .data[[mcse_col]],
      hi = est + z * .data[[mcse_col]]
    )
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.6)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = n, y = est, colour = score))
  if (!is.null(hline)) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = hline, linetype = "dashed")
  }
  if (!is.null(baseline)) {
    p <- p + geom_point(
      data = baseline,
      aes(x = n, y = random_regret),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      shape = 4, size = 3, colour = "grey40"
    )
  }
  p +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
      position = dodge, linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.3
    ) +
    geom_point(position = dodge, size = 2) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario), cols = vars(pipeline), scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = score_colours) +
    house_theme +
    labs(title = title, y = ylab, x = "sample size", colour = "Score")
}

# per-run differences between the surrogates, one box per (n, pipeline)
paired_plot <- function(df, col, title, ylab) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = n, y = .data[[col]], colour = pipeline)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "transparent", outlier.size = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~scenario, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
    house_theme +
    labs(title = title, y = ylab, x = "sample size", colour = "Pipeline")
}

head_to_head_table <- function(df, caption) {
  df %>%
    group_by(pipeline, scenario, n) %>%
    summarise(
      runs = n(),
      same_pick = mean(same_pick),
      t_better = mean(regret_diff < -1e-10),
      phi_better = mean(regret_diff > 1e-10),
      mean_diff = mean(regret_diff),
      mcse_diff = mcse_mean(regret_diff),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    kable(
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4),
      col.names = c(
        "Pipeline", "Scenario", "n", "Runs", "Same pick",
        "T-learner better", "Pseudo-outcome better",
        "Mean regret diff.", "MCSE"
      ),
      caption = caption
    )
}

# signed log for the level figure: linear within +/- sigma of zero, log
# beyond, so small and large offsets from true PEHE are both readable on one
# axis
signed_log <- scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.05, base = 10)

level_plot <- function(df, title) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = score, y = value - true_pehe, colour = score)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "transparent", outlier.shape = NA) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(scenario), cols = vars(n)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = score_colours) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      trans = signed_log,
      breaks = c(-100, -10, -1, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 1, 10, 100)
    ) +
    house_theme +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      y = "score - true PEHE (signed log scale)",
      x = NULL,
      colour = "Score"
    )
}
```

## Checks

```{r runs}
perf %>%
  filter(pi_regime == "estimated") %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, pipeline, score) %>%
  summarise(
    runs = n(),
    min_candidates = min(candidates),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, pipeline) %>%
  summarise(
    min_runs = min(runs),
    max_runs = max(runs),
    min_candidates = min(min_candidates),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = pipeline,
    values_from = c(min_runs, max_runs, min_candidates)
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = paste0(
    "Runs scored per cell (100 expected) and the fewest of the 9 candidates ",
    "ranked in any run, ", ARM, " arm, estimated propensity. A candidate is ",
    "ranked only where its score and true PEHE are both finite."
  ))
```

## 1. Which surrogate picks the better candidate?

Regret is the true PEHE of the candidate the score picks, minus the true PEHE
of the best candidate in the run. Points are means over runs with 95% Monte
Carlo intervals. The grey cross is the expected regret of picking a candidate
at random.

```{r fig-regret, fig.height=9}
selection_plot(
  filter(perf_summary, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  "mean_regret", "mcse_regret",
  title = paste0("Regret, ", ARM, " arm, estimated propensity"),
  ylab = "mean regret (PEHE)",
  baseline = random_baseline
)
```

```{r fig-rho, fig.height=9}
selection_plot(
  filter(perf_summary, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  "mean_rho", "mcse_rho",
  title = paste0("Spearman correlation with true PEHE, ", ARM, " arm, estimated propensity"),
  ylab = "mean Spearman correlation",
  hline = 0
)
```

```{r fig-top1, fig.height=9}
selection_plot(
  filter(perf_summary, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  "mean_top1", "mcse_top1",
  title = paste0("Top-1 hit rate, ", ARM, " arm, estimated propensity"),
  ylab = "share of runs picking the true best candidate",
  hline = 1 / 9
)
```

The dashed line on the top-1 figure is 1/9, a random pick.

## 2. Run by run: T-learner against pseudo-outcome

The means above can hide how often the two surrogates actually disagree. Per
run, this is the T-learner score's regret minus the pseudo-outcome score's.
Below zero, the T-learner picked the better candidate; above zero, the
pseudo-outcome did; at zero, both picked the same candidate.

```{r fig-paired-regret, fig.height=7}
paired_plot(
  filter(head_to_head, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  "regret_diff",
  title = paste0(
    "Regret, IF T-learner minus IF pseudo-outcome, per run, ", ARM,
    " arm, estimated propensity"
  ),
  ylab = "regret difference (PEHE)"
)
```

```{r paired-table}
head_to_head_table(
  filter(head_to_head, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  paste0(
    "IF T-learner against IF pseudo-outcome, per run (", ARM, " arm, ",
    "estimated propensity): share of runs where they pick the same candidate, ",
    "where each picks the strictly better one, and the mean of T-learner ",
    "regret minus pseudo-outcome regret"
  )
)
```

The same comparison on the whole ranking, not only the pick: the T-learner
score's Spearman correlation with true PEHE minus the pseudo-outcome score's.
Above zero, the T-learner ranks the 9 candidates more like the truth.

```{r fig-paired-rho, fig.height=7}
paired_plot(
  filter(head_to_head, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  "spearman_diff",
  title = paste0(
    "Spearman with true PEHE, IF T-learner minus IF pseudo-outcome, per run, ",
    ARM, " arm, estimated propensity"
  ),
  ylab = "Spearman difference"
)
```

## 3. What does each score select on?

With π = 0.5, the candidate-dependent terms of the 2019 score reduce, in
expectation, to the candidate's MSE against μ₁ rather than against τ (see
`me_metrics.R::me_per_model()`, `mu1_mse`). This is each score's Spearman
correlation, across the 9 candidates in a run, with that MSE. If one
surrogate tracks `mu1_mse` more closely than true PEHE, it is selecting on the
wrong target, not just noisily.

```{r fig-rho-mu1, fig.height=9}
selection_plot(
  filter(perf_summary, pi_regime == "estimated"),
  "mean_rho_mu1", "mcse_rho_mu1",
  title = paste0("Spearman correlation with MSE against mu1, ", ARM, " arm, estimated propensity"),
  ylab = "mean Spearman correlation",
  hline = 0
)
```

## 4. Does the score estimate PEHE itself?

The ranking measures above ignore any shift that every candidate shares. This
figure does not: it shows each candidate's score minus its true PEHE, over
runs. A score that estimates PEHE sits on zero. DR risk should sit above zero
by roughly the variance of φ about τ.

```{r fig-level-xgb, fig.height=9}
level_plot(
  filter(scores, pi_regime == "estimated", pipeline == "XGBoost"),
  paste0("Score minus true PEHE, ", ARM, " arm, XGBoost, estimated propensity")
)
```

```{r level-table}
scores %>%
  filter(pi_regime == "estimated") %>%
  group_by(pipeline, score, n) %>%
  summarise(bias = mean(value - true_pehe, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = n, values_from = bias, names_prefix = "n = ") %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = paste0(
    "Mean of score minus true PEHE, over scenarios, runs and candidates (",
    ARM, " arm, estimated propensity)"
  ))
```

## 5. Population check: oracle nuisances

From `me_infl_investigation.R`: N = 2·10⁶ draws per scenario,
**oracle** nuisances (true μ₀, μ₁ and π = 0.5), five constructed candidates
(the truth, the ATE, the truth shrunk halfway to the ATE, μ₁, and τ + X2).
With oracle nuisances the T-learner surrogate μ₁ − μ₀ is the true τ, so "IF,
true tau" is the noise-free version of the T-learner score. A correct PEHE
estimator lies on the diagonal, and a correct ranking is at least monotone in
true PEHE. The One-step score uses a deliberately biased surrogate,
τ + 0.3·X2, so its gap from the diagonal is the second-order remainder the
correction leaves behind.

```{r fig-population, fig.height=7}
pop_labels <- c(
  dr = "DR risk",
  onestep_biased_sur = "One-step (biased surrogate)",
  infl_tau = "IF, true tau",
  infl_phi = "IF, pseudo-outcome"
)

population %>%
  pivot_longer(
    any_of(names(pop_labels)),
    names_to = "score", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    score = factor(pop_labels[score], levels = unname(pop_labels)),
    scenario = factor(
      scenario_labels[as.character(scenario)],
      levels = unname(scenario_labels)
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(scenario, score, true_pehe) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = true_pehe, y = value, colour = score)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe") +
  house_theme +
  labs(
    title = "Score against true PEHE, oracle nuisances",
    x = "true PEHE", y = "score", colour = "Score"
  )
```

## Appendix

### Fixed propensity (π = 0.5)

The DGM assigns treatment by a fair coin, so π = 0.5 is the true propensity
and these are oracle-π versions of every score. Thesis Table `me_if_selection`
is the XGBoost column of this regime.

```{r fig-regret-fixed, fig.height=9}
selection_plot(
  filter(perf_summary, pi_regime == "fixed"),
  "mean_regret", "mcse_regret",
  title = paste0("Regret, ", ARM, " arm, propensity fixed at 0.5"),
  ylab = "mean regret (PEHE)",
  baseline = random_baseline
)
```

```{r fig-paired-regret-fixed, fig.height=7}
paired_plot(
  filter(head_to_head, pi_regime == "fixed"),
  "regret_diff",
  title = paste0(
    "Regret, IF T-learner minus IF pseudo-outcome, per run, ", ARM,
    " arm, propensity fixed at 0.5"
  ),
  ylab = "regret difference (PEHE)"
)
```

```{r paired-table-fixed}
head_to_head_table(
  filter(head_to_head, pi_regime == "fixed"),
  paste0(
    "IF T-learner against IF pseudo-outcome, per run (", ARM, " arm, ",
    "propensity fixed at 0.5)"
  )
)
```

```{r fig-level-fixed, fig.height=9}
level_plot(
  filter(scores, pi_regime == "fixed", pipeline == "XGBoost"),
  paste0("Score minus true PEHE, ", ARM, " arm, XGBoost, propensity fixed at 0.5")
)
```

### AutoML pipeline, level

```{r fig-level-automl, fig.height=9}
level_plot(
  filter(scores, pi_regime == "estimated", pipeline == "AutoML"),
  paste0("Score minus true PEHE, ", ARM, " arm, AutoML, estimated propensity")
)
```
